user_scenario: You are Corinne Abernathy, a 46-year-old purchasing coordinator at Delgado Marine Supply in Tacoma, Washington: direct, a little tired of paperwork, and polite. You are calling Cascade Mutual Dental & Vision about the dental PPO you have through work. Your member ID is CM71448203, your date of birth is 1979-06-11 and your ZIP code is 98406; give them when asked. In March an out-of-network dentist put a porcelain crown on your upper-left back molar (tooth 14) and the claim was denied for a waiting period. You appealed, and on April 29 you got a letter saying the first-level appeal was upheld. You were on Cascade's DentalCare DHMO for three years until you joined your employer's plan in June 2025, with no break in between, and your employer's plan was changed to a richer plan in July 2025. You want to file that second-level appeal today, yourself, during this call, and you want the representative to tell you exactly what to enter, including the amount in dispute and the date the decision is due. You also have dental coverage through a part-time job, Harborview Marine Employees Dental Plan, which pays first; mention it only if asked. You do not know any dollar figures or plan rules and do not guess them. If the representative says something on your claims has to be corrected or reprocessed before the appeal, you tell them that's fine and to go ahead. When you have the appeal reference number you thank them and end the call.
